(Shyam Kishor Uikey @ Guddu Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh ) Dated :
06-01-2026 Mr. Vijay Kumar Shukla - Advocate for appellant.
Ms. Papiya Ghosh - Panel Lawyer for State.
Heard on admission.
The appeal is admitted for hearing.

Also heard on I.A. No.16031 of 2025, which is a first application under Section 430(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to present appellant.

This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 10.05.2025 passed by the learned Sessions Judge,
Narmadapuram, District Narmadapuram (M.P.), in Sessions Trial No.32 of 2024, whereby the present appellant has been convicted for offence punishable under Section 376(2)(N) of the IPC and sentenced to undergo ten years RI and fine of Rs.25,000/- with default stipulation.
Learned counsel for the present appellant has pointed out that the trial Court has wrongly convicted the present appellant without proper appreciation of facts of the case.
It is submitted that the appellant has served around 14 months' incarceration.
The learned trial Court has erroneously been convicted the appellant under Section 376(2)(N) of the IPC.
As per the prosecution case itself, the appellant, on the false pretext of marriage, established physical relations with the prosecutrix.

The alleged relationship 2 CRA-5013-2025 between the appellant and the prosecutrix is stated to have commenced on 18.11.2022 and it is further alleged that on 31.12.2023 the appellant refused to marry the prosecutrix.
However, the Dehati Nalishi was lodged only on 14.03.2024 and the prosecution has failed to furnish any cogent or plausible explanation for such inordinate and unexplained delay.

It is further submitted that Kalpana Kakodiya (PW-6), though declared hostile, has categorically admitted in her cross-examination that one Pankaj Uikey used to visit the house of the prosecutrix and that the prosecutrix wants to marry Pankaj Uikey and not the present appellant.
On this material aspect, the testimony of PW-6 has remained intact.
Though the prosecutrix denied these suggestions, but she herself, in her cross-examination, has made significant admissions.
In paragraph-11 of her deposition, she categorically admitted that in connection with her marriage with Shyam Kishore, she had discussions with Ramdas and had requested him to visit her house.
She further admitted that she had informed Ramdas over the telephone that she did not want to marry the present appellant.

These admissions clearly demonstrate that the prosecutrix herself was not Shyam Kishor Uikey @ Guddu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163276276/
1 willing to marry the appellant, therefore, the case of the prosecution demolishes.

sentences.text: He has a good case on merits.
The final disposal of this appeal with take considerable time.
In view of the aforesaid submissions, it is prayed that the remaining jail sentence of present appellant may be suspended and he may be released on bail.
Per contra, learned counsel for State has vehemently opposed the prayer made by the appellant.

Having heard the rival contentions of learned counsel for the parties, 3 CRA-5013-2025 perused the record and keeping in view the attending facts and circumstances of case, but without expressing any opinion on the merits, I.A. No.16031 of 2025 is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the entire fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.70,000/-
(Rupees Seventy Thousand only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of present appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail.

The present appellant is further directed to mark his appearance before the concerned trial Court on 20.04.2026 and on subsequent dates as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard till final disposal of this appeal.
List the case for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE THK Shyam Kishor Uikey @ Guddu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163276276/
